BUGS: (a) listTrailing pending-entry-requests block is hidden whenever the displayed bib list is empty (CardListPanel.tsx:135-148 — listTrailing only renders in the non-empty else-branch; showEmpty short-circuits it). (b) CSL preview (getFormattedBib/formatBibliography) is threaded everywhere but never rendered in the card body — dead feature. (d) duplicate-citekey silent drop on display (sortedEntries seen-set :220-235).

Bibliography card bodies render ONLY plain .bib field text (BibEntryCard.tsx:248-287, escaped JSX) + a free-HTML annotation editor — there is NO BorrowedMainText/RichTextField surface and NO embedded citation/footnote/\ref/inline-math atoms inside the body, so atom-click-through-from-body is structurally absent. One body-render security defect found and filed under F5 (annotation innerHTML sink, BIB-F5-01) since it lives in the edit path, not a nested-atom path.

Edit body (annotation), title (header is read-only derived from fields, not directly editable), named fields (@type/key/fields inline editor), AI-request flag (Request review for fields/notes). Multiple defects: annotation editor injects unsanitized innerHTML (XSS sink); AI-completed annotation/fields never re-appear without a full doc reload (no annotations re-read, AnnotationEditor seeds only on bibKey); citekey rename does not propagate to the editor's live \cite; inline field editor can't add fields and can't delete fields (merge-only); 'complete' review status has no UI affordance and re-files a duplicate request.

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: When the displayed bibliography list is empty (e.g. 'Cited entries only' before any citation exists, or a search with no matches), the user's pending 'Request entry' items silently vanish from the panel — they only reappear once at least one entry is displayed.
findings.suspectedRootCause: CardListPanel renders `listTrailing` only inside the non-empty `else` branch. `showEmpty = items.length === 0 && !hasAiRequests && emptyState != null` (CardListPanel.tsx:112) is computed without regard to `listTrailing`; when true the component returns the emptyState alone and never reaches the branch that emits `aiRequestsSection` + items + `listTrailing` (lines 135-149). Bibliography passes its Pending-requests block as `listTrailing` (BibliographyPanel.tsx:837-876,907), so an empty list buries it.

evidence.note: showEmpty ignores listTrailing presence
emptyState returned alone; listTrailing (line 148) is in the else branch only
entryRequests rendered via listTrailing, so hidden when displayedEntries is empty

reproSteps: Open a paper with no citations yet (or set filter to 'Cited entries only').
Open the Add menu → 'Request entry', submit a description.
The pending request appears below the (empty) list — actually it does NOT: the list has 0 displayed entries so the empty-state text shows and the Pending requests block is suppressed.
Switch filter to 'Full bibliography' so at least one entry shows → the pending request reappears.
findings.suspectedClass: Any panel that uses CardListPanel `listTrailing` for content that should survive an empty item list. Same trap would hit any future trailing-section content; the structural fix is to render `listTrailing` outside the showEmpty gate (or fold it into the empty calculation).

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: The CSL-formatted bibliography preview that the panel's `getFormattedBib` prop implies (the brief lists it as a bibliography function) is never shown anywhere — there is no formatted-citation rendering in the card.
findings.suspectedRootCause: `getFormattedBib` is declared in BibEntryCardProps (BibEntryCard.tsx:19), destructured in the component (line 146), and threaded through every host/float path (bibliography-host.tsx:53, cards/floats/index.tsx:469,515) but is referenced nowhere in the render body — the only formatted output rendered is the hand-built publication-details JSX row (lines 248-287), which never calls formatBibliography/getFormattedBib. The CSL preview feature is unimplemented/dead.

evidence.note: getFormattedBib destructured but never called below
getFormattedBib = formatBibliography(entry, style) — computed but its only consumer never renders it
prop forwarded into the float too, equally unused

reproSteps: Open a Bibliography card and expand it.
Observe BibTeX Fields + Annotations pods but no CSL-formatted reference string anywhere.
Grep BibEntryCard.tsx for getFormattedBib — only the destructure, no usage.
findings.suspectedClass: Dead prop threaded through panel→host→float. Sibling risk: any card prop that survives a refactor but loses its render site (e.g. occurrence/jump props on other cards) — same audit pattern of 'prop exists, never read'.

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: An entry with a very long title produces a tall multi-line header even in the compressed (collapsed, unselected) card state, breaking the uniform compressed-card height across the strip.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The header line (author·year·title) is styled `flex-1 min-w-0 leading-snug` with `overflowWrap: anywhere` (BibEntryCard.tsx:476-489) but has no `truncate`/`line-clamp`. The CardDisplay compressed-lines mechanism (DOCKED_COMPRESSED_LINES) only governs the card *body*; the header always renders in full, and `compressed` (line 449) only gates the body+separator (line 567). So a long title wraps unbounded in collapsed mode.

evidence.note: header div: flex-1 min-w-0 leading-snug, no clamp
compressed gates only the body, not the header
{!compressed && (body+separator)} — header is outside this gate, always full

reproSteps: Add a .bib entry with a 200-char title.
View it collapsed in the Bibliography panel (not selected).
Header wraps to several lines; collapsed card is much taller than its neighbors.
findings.suspectedClass: Other card headers that derive a single-line summary from arbitrary user/.bib text without a clamp (citation header, footnote bodyTitle) — check whether their compressed summary clamps the header line specifically.

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: If two .bib entries share a citekey, only the first is ever displayed; the second is silently dropped from both the list and the cited.bib export.
findings.suspectedRootCause: `sortedEntries` dedupes via a `seen` Set keyed on `e.key` (BibliographyPanel.tsx:220-235) and `handleExportCited` repeats the same `seen` filter (:350-355). A genuine duplicate-key entry never reaches the user. (Note: the parser's `extractRawEntries` already collapses duplicates by lowercased key into a Record (bib-parser.ts:854-877), so in practice the second raw block is usually lost upstream — but citation-js `cite.data` can still emit two CSL items, in which case the panel-level dedup is the visible drop.)

evidence.note: filter drops e when seen.has(e.key) — silent
export repeats the same seen-set drop
extractRawEntries keys raw by lowercased citekey — collapses duplicates upstream too

reproSteps: Hand-edit references.bib to contain two @article entries with the same citekey but different fields.
Open the Bibliography panel — only one entry shows, no warning.
Export cited.bib — only one block emitted.
findings.suspectedClass: Silent seen-set dedup is the lead-#5 class; the empty-`raw` `.filter(Boolean)` export drop (handleExportCited :363) is the sibling — an entry whose `raw` is '' (e.g. assembled in-memory, or library-add with raw cleared) is silently omitted from cited.bib while still counting in the list.

findings.suspectedRootCause: AnnotationEditor sets the contentEditable content with `editorRef.current.innerHTML = content || ''` (BibEntryCard.tsx:113) with no sanitization. `content` is the raw annotation string from annotations.json, which is written by the answer-bib-review skill (type:notes → annotations.json) and travels with a shared paper. findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: After the AI completes a bib-review (notes or fields), the freshly-written annotation / corrected fields do not appear in the open Bibliography panel — the pending pill clears, but the content stays stale until the user closes and reopens the doc.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Two independent refresh gaps: (1) Annotations — useAnnotations reads annotations.json once per docId via usePersistentState (no poll, no event listener; useAnnotations.ts:13-19) and AnnotationEditor only re-seeds innerHTML on a `[bibKey]` change (BibEntryCard.tsx:111-115), so a newly-written annotation for the same open key never re-renders. (2) Fields — useCitations re-reads the .bib only on DOC_BIB_CHANGED_EVENT (useCitations.ts:137-147), which is dispatched solely by in-app project-bib writes (project-bib.ts:72,129); the answer-bib-review skill writes references.bib on disk out-of-band and fires no such event, and there is no FS-watch. Meanwhile useBibReview DOES poll bib-review-requests.json every 10s (useBibReview.ts:42-48), so the 'Requested' pill clears — producing the misleading 'done but unchanged' state.

evidence.note: usePersistentState — loads once per docId, no poll/event for external annotation writes
AnnotationEditor seeds innerHTML only when bibKey changes — same-key content update is ignored
bib re-read gated on DOC_BIB_CHANGED_EVENT only
the only dispatchers of DOC_BIB_CHANGED_EVENT are in-app library drops — not an external skill .bib write
10s poll clears the pending pill, creating the stale-but-marked-done state

reproSteps: Open a bib entry, click 'Request annotation' (notes) or 'Request review' (fields) and keep the card open.
Run the answer-bib-review skill so it writes annotations.json / references.bib and flips the request to complete.
Within 10s the pending pill clears, but the Annotations body / BibTeX Fields still show the OLD content.
Reload the doc → the AI content finally appears.
findings.suspectedClass: All sidecars/.bib written out-of-band by editor skills but only loaded once per docId or refreshed on a narrowly-dispatched in-app event (no FS-watch). Sibling: any panel relying on a contentEditable seeded once on mount (AnnotationEditor pattern) won't reflect an external same-key content change.

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: Renaming a citekey via a bib card's 'Edit entry' changes the .bib key and the citations.json sidecar, but every live \cite{oldKey} in the editor keeps the old key — so those in-text citations now point at a missing entry and render as '??', and on the next editor parse the sidecar rewrite is reverted.
findings.suspectedRootCause: updateBibKeyAndType (useCitations.ts:281-315) rewrites the .bib entry and then rewrites the sidecar citations' `command`/`keys` via a `\b`-bounded regex (lines 299-311). But the editor's \cite node text in the .tex is the source of truth: syncFromEditor regenerates citation ids and rebuilds the sidecar from the editor on every parse (useCitations.ts:352-374, and the doc comment there confirms 'editor regenerates citation ids on each parse'). Nothing in updateBibKeyAndType dispatches an editor transaction to rewrite \cite{oldKey}→\cite{newKey} in the doc. So the sidecar edit is cosmetic and transient, and the in-text citation is orphaned against the renamed entry.

evidence.note: rename only patches sidecar command/keys, never the editor doc
syncFromEditor rebuilds citations from the editor and DROPS prior ids — overwrites the sidecar rename on next parse
commitEditBib calls onUpdateBibKeyAndType when the key changes — the panel's only rename entry point
formatInlineCitation returns '??' author when map.get(key) is undefined — what the orphaned \cite{oldKey} now renders

reproSteps: Cite an entry in the body (\cite{smith2020}).
Open that entry in the Bibliography panel, 'Edit entry', change key smith2020 → smith2020a, Save.
The .bib now has smith2020a; the in-text citation still says \cite{smith2020} and renders as '?? (year)'.
Type anything to trigger a reparse → the sidecar rename is gone too.
findings.suspectedClass: Any panel-side mutation of a value whose source of truth is the editor doc (citekeys, footnote text, labels) that only patches the sidecar and not the PM doc — it will be silently reverted by the next syncFromEditor/observer pass. The deep fix is to route citekey renames through an editor transaction, mirroring how the find-citation/sync-bib skills rewrite \cite in the .tex.

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: The inline BibTeX-fields editor can neither add a new field (e.g. supply a missing DOI) nor remove an existing one — clearing a field to blank leaves an empty `field = {}` in the .bib rather than deleting it.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The edit form only iterates the entry's EXISTING fields (BibEntryCard.tsx:362-369 maps Object.entries(editBibFields), seeded from {...entry.fields}); there is no UI to append a key. On Save, commitEditBib calls onUpdateBibEntry(entry.key, editBibFields) which MERGES (useCitations.ts:265: `{ ...e.fields, ...fields }`) — a field the user blanked is written through as an empty string, never deleted, and the serializer then emits `field = {}`.

evidence.note: edit form only renders existing fields; no add-field affordance
commitEditBib passes editBibFields wholesale to onUpdateBibEntry
merge semantics: `{ ...e.fields, ...fields }` — cleared field persists as '' rather than being removed

reproSteps: Open an entry missing a DOI, 'Edit entry' — there is no row to add `doi`.
Clear the `pages` field to empty and Save.
Inspect references.bib — the entry now contains `pages = {}` rather than dropping the field.
findings.suspectedClass: Merge-only field updaters across the bib/card edit surface (any onUpdate that spreads new over old without honoring deletions); the answer-bib-review skill's 'replace-all-fields' mode (answer-bib-review.md:109-115) exists precisely because set-fields can't delete — the manual UI lacks that escape hatch.

findings.subject: bibliography
findings.symptom: Once a bib-review is marked 'complete', the card gives no completion affordance — the request button reverts to its idle 'Request review' label, and clicking it files a brand-new pending request rather than acknowledging the finished one.
findings.suspectedRootCause: BibEntryCard branches the request UI only on `=== 'pending'` (BibEntryCard.tsx:320-328, 408-416 and handleRequestToggle :222-235). getReviewStatus can return 'complete' (useBibReview.ts:96-103; the type is enumerated 'none'|'pending'|'complete') but the card treats 'complete' identically to 'none' — idle label, and handleRequestToggle's else-branch re-files via onRequestReview. There is no 'reviewed' badge and no path to clear a completed row from the card (only clearRequest exists in the hook, unused by the card).

evidence.note: handleRequestToggle only special-cases 'pending'; 'complete' falls into the re-request else
pill label/style only checks fieldsReviewStatus === 'pending'
getRequestStatus can return 'complete' — never reflected in the card

reproSteps: Request a fields review on an entry; let the AI complete it (status → complete).
After the 10s poll, the button shows 'Request review' again (no 'reviewed' indication).
Click it — a fresh pending request is filed for the already-completed entry.
findings.suspectedClass: Tri-state status (none/pending/complete) collapsed to a binary pending/not check at the UI; any other card consuming a 'complete' status without a distinct rendering (citation bib-review, report-request fulfillment) risks the same re-fire-on-complete behavior.
